Sir,

Acting under instructions of Mr. Charles Madar, I have the ho-
nour to approach you on the following subject:-

My client is a sole proprietor and owner of the Radio Station un-
der the name of "X H H G Radio Broadcast Station", 731 Canton Road (120
Yu Ya Ching Road) as per a Bill of Sale dated December 2nd, 1938, and
duly registered at H. B. M. Consulate-General at Shanghai on the 12th
of December, 1938, under No. 607. A copy of said Bill of Sale has been
duly deposited by me at the Office of the Headquarters of the Shanghai
Municipal Police. The said Radio Station is operating on 1220 K.C. But
some time ago it was established by my client that some other Radio
Station is using the same kilocycle causing thereby harm and confusion
to interests of my client. As a certain Mei Sung Radio Station, 432 Nan-
king Road, announced in Chinese Press some time ago that it will use
said kilocycle my client suspects that the Radio Station in question is
said Mei Sung Radio Station.

Under those circumstances I have the honour to request you to in-
vestigate the matter and to take necessary steps in order to stop, if
it is possible, such activity in future or to let me know the name and

Date December 12, 1938.

Subject Tung Fang Broadcasting Station: Ownership transferred to
Mr. Charles Madar (British), 259 Kiangse Road
Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Crawford

At 3.30 p.m., December 12, 1938, Mr. N.A. Ivanow,
Attorney and Counsellor-at-Law, 153-L, Apt. 53, Route des
Soeurs, called at Headquarters, and handed over a copy of
a bill of sale, which is registered as Miscellaneous
Document No. 607, dated December 12, 1938, at the British
Consulate-General, in respect of the sale of the Tung Fang
Broadcasting Station (XHHG). K.C.1220 to Charles Madar
(British), 259 Kiangse Road, which transaction took place
on December 2, 1938.

The Tung Fang Station is one of the few Chinese
Stations which refused to register with the Japanese after
the retreat of the Chinese forces from the Shanghai area.

Reference Special Branch Report dated 9-12-38, a
report appeared in the December 5th issue of the Sin Wan
Pao announcing that a new Broadcasting Station to be known
as the Mei Sung (美聲) Station, K.C.1220 will commence
broadcasting soon, from 423 Nanking Road. It will be noted
that K.C.1220 is the wavelength over which the Tung Fang
Station broadcasts. Up to date, efforts to locate the
owner of the proposed Mei Sung Station have proved
unsuccessful.

Logan
D. S. I.

D.C. (Special Branch).

主题 东方广播电台：所有权转让给查尔斯·马达尔先生（英籍），江西路259号
由副督察长 洛根 (Logan) 制作，由 C. Crawford 转呈

1938年12月12日下午3时30分，N.A. Ivanow 先生，律师及法律顾问，住址姐妹路 (Route des Soeurs) 153-L号，53室，来到总部，递交了一份卖据副本，该卖据作为第607号杂项文件，于1938年12月12日在英国总领事馆注册，内容涉及将东方广播电台 (XHHG)，频率1220千周 (K.C.) 出售给查尔斯·马达尔（英籍），住址江西路259号，该交易发生于1938年12月2日。

东方电台是少数在中国军队撤出上海地区后拒绝向日本人注册的中文电台之一。

参照日期为38年12月9日的特别科报告，《新闻报》(Sin Wan Pao) 12月5日刊出一则报道，宣布一家名为美声 (Mei Sung) 的新广播电台，频率1220千周 (K.C.)，即将从南京路423号开始广播。值得注意的是，1220千周 (K.C.) 正是东方电台广播所使用的波长。截至目前，寻找拟议中的美声电台所有者的努力均未成功。

洛根

Subject Tung Fang Radio Broadcasting Station (XHHA) - frequency
changed from K.C. 1080 to K.C. 1220.
Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Crawford. S.S.

* Sec-D6813/14/II
- Aerial No. 12

Reference Special Branch Report dated 19.7.38 on above
subject and remarks of Commissioner of Police thereon, on
24.7.38, the attached letter dated 24.7.38 was received from
the management of the Tung Fang (東方) Station intimating
their intention to change the frequency of their Station
from K.C. 1080 to K.C. 1060. As this frequency had already
been adopted by the Chung Ih Station (Italian), the Tung Fang
Station was informed that they should choose a vacant frequency.
On 26.7.38, another letter dated 26.7.38 (attached) was received
at Special Branch, Headquarters, intimating that K.C. 1220
which is vacant, has been adopted by the Tung Fang Station.
The management of the Tung Fang Station was subsequently
informed that there is no Police objection to the change,
whereupon they' intimated that the change would be effected
within one week's time, as it is necessary to advertise the
alteration. It is suggested that the Broadcasting Superintend-
ence Office be informed of the change in order to obviate the
possibility of K.C. 1220 being assigned by the latter organ
to another station.

Logan
D. S. I.

D.C. (Special Branch)

P.A. to D.C. (Sp. Br.)

the Tung Fang Radio Station (call sign XMHG - 1080 K.C.)

the stations which the Japanese authorities desire the
Police to warn to apply for a Japanese permit.

of the Wu Kung Lodging House, 152 Fokien Road while the

Made by D.S.I. Logan, Forwarded by C. Crawford D.I.

On March 17, 1939, Mr. W. Gunndellach,
representing Mr. Carl Wacker (German), foreign manager
of the proposed Sino-German Broadcasting Station
(X.H.C.E.) K.C.580, Room 617, Continental Emporium
Building, Lane 353, Nanking Road, called at Headquarters
and stated that he had approached the Japanese Radio
Control Office and had been informed that no new
stations would be permitted by the Japanese to commence
operating and requested advice as to what action the
Police would take should the proposed Sino-German
Station commence to operate without a permit from the
Japanese. Mr. Gunndellach was informed that according
to an agreement between the S.M.P. and the Japanese
Radio Control Office, new radio stations would not be
permitted to operate by the Police until a permit had
been issued by the Japanese, whereupon he left stating
that he would convey the information mentioned to Mr.
Wacker. On 18.3.39, the attached letters from Mr. Wacker
were delivered to D.S.I. Logan by registered mail,
intimating that the Sino-German station will begin to
operate in course of the next week.

It should be noted that the proposed station
is in reality Chinese owned and that Mr. Wacker is
merely the nominal manager. According to the existing
practice all radio stations which are owned by persons
not enjoying extra-territorial rights, apart from the
prerequisite of obtaining the sanction of the Japanese,
should also furnish to the S.M.P. a guarantee not to

1939年3月17日，代表拟议中的中德广播电台（X.H.C.E.）580千周外籍经理卡尔·瓦克先生（德国人）的 W. Gunndellach 先生来到总部，地址为南京路353弄大陆商场大楼617室。他表示已接触日本无线电管制办公室，并被告知日本方面不允许新电台开始运营，并询问如果拟议的中德电台在未获得日本许可证的情况下开始运营，警方将采取何种行动。告知 Gunndellach 先生，根据上海公共租界工部局警务处与日本无线电管制办公室之间的协议，在日本颁发许可证之前，警方不允许新广播电台运营。随后他离开，表示会将上述信息转达给瓦克先生。1939年3月18日，瓦克先生的附函通过挂号信送达副督察长洛根，暗示中德电台将于下周内开始运营。

值得注意的是，拟议中的电台实际上由中国人所有，瓦克先生仅是名义上的经理。根据现行惯例，所有由不享有治外法权的人士拥有的广播电台，除了必须获得日本方面的批准这一先决条件外，还应向上海公共租界工部局警务处提供担保，承诺不

17. THE BUND.
SHANGHAI.

March 17, 1939.

Dear Mr. Logan,

Through the good offices of Mr. Gundelach I received yesterday his report after his visit to the Japanese Superintendent's Radio Control Station office in the Hardoon Building and his consequent call and the ensuing conversation at your office.
Gundelach told me exactly how matters stand concerning the running of broadcast stations in the Settlement and I think my Chinese will not experience any difficulties with the authorities as long as they confine their activities to purely commercial advertising broadcasts.
Taking into consideration the mentality of the Chinese and to convince them that as far as the Settlement regulations are concerned everything has been done to enable them of starting their business without obstructions, I beg to enclose my information in writing stating that the Sino German Broadcast Station under letters XHCE, running on 580 kilocycles will begin business in the course of next week.
All I require from you are a few lines confirming receipt of this communication (with no reference whatsoever regarding the Japanese).
May I ask you to kindly send your letter to my private address:

A representative of Mr. Wacker, namely
Mr. W. Gunndellach (German), employed by Hickhoff &
Co., 20 Canton Road, was interviewed at Headquarters
on 13/3/39, when he stated that Mr. Wacker had been
approached by a Chinese friend, Mr. N.C. Chang, afore-
said and asked if he would assume the managership of
the proposed Radio Station. Mr. Wacker agreed to do
so on condition that he would not be held responsible
for the conduct of the station should friction arise
with either the Settlement Authorities or the Japanese
Authorities.

Office in respect of the proposed station after which

Reference D.C. (Special Branch's) memo.
dated 20.6.39 in reference to above, Mr. V. Chieri
was interviewed at Police Headquarters on the morning
of June 22, 1939 when he was informed of the fact
that K.C. 880 was adopted by Mr. Francois Lesspinasse
(French) as far back as December, 1938 and that Mr.
Lespinasse's station has been functioning for some
time. In reply, Mr. Chieri stated that he did not
wish to come into conflict either with Mr. Lespinasse
or the authorities as he is well known in Shanghai
and is a member of the French Police (Specials) and
that he would not commence broadcasting without
notifying the Police. In the meantime, however,
he stated his intention to approach the Japanese
Broadcasting Control Office with a view to obtaining
that organ's permission to use one of the wavelengths
reserved by the Japanese so far not in use. In
conclusion he stated that should the Japanese allocate
a wavelength to him, he will refer same to the Police
in order to ascertain if it is not already in use by
any other person.

asked whether he had approached the Japanese Radio
Control Office in connection with this matter and on
replying in the negative Mr. Maslovsky was given to
understand that owing to lack of space on the wave
band there was practically no hope of his application
being approved.

Communicated with by the undersigned on
21-9-39 Mr. Maslovsky stated that so far he had not
approached the Japanese Radio Control Office as he
decided to await a reply from the Municipal Police
before doing so. Furthermore he stated that he had
failed to come to an agreement with the Sokol Club,
888 Weihaiwei Road, regarding the use of their
premises and that he was still looking for suitable
premises for his proposed station.

According to Maslovsky, he intends to
operate the proposed radio station in partnership
with V.I. Yakovleff, engineer, but he alone will be
responsible for conducting the station in accordance
with the conditions under which registration will be
approved. The broadcasting programme will consist of

DIPL. ING ELEKTROTECHNIK
64 Rt. Pichon Apt. 10.
29th of August 1939 .
To the President of Russian Emigrant Committee.
Sir,
I have the honour to apply to Chinese Ministry of Communications
for a license on my name to operate a broadcasting radio station.
This broadcasting station has been situated on 1074 Bubbling Well
Road and commenced its operation on 2nd of April 1939. The license was
obtained from Shanghai Municipal Authorities on the name of a British
subject, Mr. Bosustow. After two months operation Mr. Bosustow was
informed by Mr. Acano of Ministry of Communications about necessity to
register the station. After that Mr. Bosustow ceased to continue the
operation of this station.
As I have obtained from owner all the rights to operate this station
on my name, so I beg to point out that this station will be used for
commercial and cultural purposes only and will be of great interest to
the Russian Colony here, therefore the broadcasting will be mostly on
Russian language. The program will consist of musical numbers, education-
al lectures and commercial advertisements and in no way be used in any
kind of political propaganda.
I have the honour to apply to you as the head of Russian Emigrant
Committee to be so kind as to assist me in this matter to obtain the
necessary permission to operate broadcasting station. This station will
be entirely a Russian enterprise and will enable a few Russian to earn
their living.
I remain, Sir,
Your obedient servant
Dipl. Eng. S. Maslovsky.

先生：
我很荣幸向中华民国交通部申请以我的名义颁发经营无线电广播电台的执照。
该广播电台位于静安寺路1074号，并于1939年4月2日开始运营。执照是以英国臣民 Bosustow（博苏斯托）先生的名义从上海市政当局获得的。运营两个月后，交通部 Acano（音译）先生通知 Bosustow（博苏斯托）先生必须注册该电台。此后，Bosustow（博苏斯托）先生停止继续运营该电台。
既然我已从业主处获得以我的名义运营该电台的所有权利，因此我恳请指出，该电台将仅用于商业和文化目的，并将引起此处俄罗斯侨民社区的极大兴趣，因此广播将主要使用俄语。节目将包括音乐曲目、教育讲座和商业广告，绝不用于任何形式的政治宣传。
我很荣幸向您作为俄罗斯侨民委员会的主席提出申请，恳请您在此事上协助我，以获得经营广播电台的必要许可。该电台将完全是一家俄罗斯企业，并使少数俄罗斯人得以谋生。
谨此致敬，

先生，
您顺从的仆人
电机工程师 S. Maslovsky（马斯洛夫斯基）。

In connection with the Charity Bazaar scheduled for July 1, 2 and 3 at the Ningpo Fellow Countrymen's Association, it is learned that this Association received a threatening letter, the details of which are as follows:-

At 8.10.p.m. June 25th, 1939, an unknown male Chinese in foreign style clothing, answering the description of the man described on Sheet 1 of Diary 1, called at the Ningpo Fellow Countrymen's Association, 480 Yu Ya Ching Road, and delivered a letter addressed to the Management, to a coolie named Wu Sung Sung (鄔申生) who was standing at the front door at the time. The letter was later seen by the executives of the Association. It purports to have emanated from a "Chinese Kuomintang Youth's Anti-Communist Iron & Blood Group (中国国民党青年反共铁血团)" and warns the Association against leasing its premises for the use of a charity bazaar, on pain of drastic measures.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Enclosed in the letter was one 7.63 bullet.

A summarized translation of the letter is given hereunder:-

"Ningpo Fellow Countrymen's Association:

It is learned that a charity bazaar will be held in your premises. The bazaar is sponsored by Communist and "Popular Front" elements, who are defrauding the people in the name of "Relief Work". We therefore wish to reveal their intrigues. You are hereby instructed to refuse the leasing of the premises to that bazaar, failing which drastic measures will be adopted. It will greatly harm you. A bullet is enclosed to serve as a warning to you.

Chinese Kuomintang Youth's Anti-Communist Iron & Blood Group."

Receipt of the letter was reported to S.M.P. Special Branch on the morning of June 27th, the Management of the Association being then requested to report the case to Louza Station but they, however, failed to do so.

Consequently on the morning of 29-6-39, C.D.C.37 and the undersigned proceeded to the Ningpo Guild and there interviewed Mr. Yu Tung Kong (虞東康) who is in charge of the leasing of halls and rooms in the Association. He handed over the letter and bullet to the undersigned but stated that the Association did not desire that Police take any action in the case.

Translation of a pamphlet, copies of which were
distributed from the 5th floor of the Sun Company
Building on Nanking Road near Lloyd Road at 1.40 p.m.
on 28/6/39.

This is to inform the Shanghai Citizens about the
holding of The Exhibition of Articles for Charity
Sale sponsored by the Shanghai Chinese Professional
Women's Club.

Racket behind the activities of
National Salvation Association
revealed; Local citizens warned
to guard against being deceived.

Brethren!

Another "Exhibition of Articles for Charity Sale" is now
being held at the Ningpo Fellow Countrymen's Association by the
Shanghai Chinese Professional Women's Club with office in Room
203, upper floor of the Hall & Holtz Building, 120 Nanking Road,
which has been sponsored and inaugurated by the People's Front
Organization, otherwise known as the National Salvation Associa-
tion. This is another of their rackets aiming at deceiving
the people behind the mask of charity. For the sake of justice,
we, who have been repeatedly deceived by them, cannot but raise
our voice and reveal their intrigues and selfish activities!

The task of giving relief to refugees, we should indeed
carry out to the best of our ability. But such task involving
as it does no small amount of difficulties, should be handled
and controlled by the competent authorities so that the possi-
bility of unscrupulous elements seeking their own selfish ends
under the guise of and in the name of charity, may be excluded.
Organizations such as the International Relief Committee, and
the Shanghai Refugee Relief Association, are the proper organs
responsible for the relief of refugees; they have been brought
into being by local respectable civil organs and are being
maintained in accordance with legal principles. The present
exhibition of articles for a charity sale, and other forms of
charity bazaars are nothing more than the selfish means whereby
page_data.zh:
1939年6月28日下午1时40分，在南京路近劳合氏路（Lloyd Road）的新新公司大楼五楼分发的小册子译文。

特此告知上海市民，上海中国职业妇女俱乐部将举办慈善义卖物品展览会。

揭露救国会活动背后的
敲诈勒索勾当；
警告本地市民谨防受骗。

同胞们！

上海中国职业妇女俱乐部（办事处位于南京路120号哈尔与霍尔茨大楼（Hall & Holtz Building）楼上203室）目前正在宁波同乡会举办另一场“慈善义卖物品展览会”，该活动由人民阵线组织（又称救国会）赞助并发起。这是他们以慈善为幌子欺骗人民的又一敲诈勾当。为了正义起见，我们这些屡次受其欺骗的人不得不发出呼声，揭露他们的阴谋和自私行径！

救济难民的工作，我们确实应尽力而为。但这项工作涉及不少困难，应由主管当局处理和控制，以排除不肖之徒借慈善之名行利己之实的可能性。国际救济委员会和上海难民救济协会等组织是负责难民救济的适当机构；它们由本地受人尊敬的民间团体组建，并依法维持运作。目前的慈善义卖物品展览及其他形式的慈善义卖市集，不过是

page_data.en:
- 2 -

the People's Front Organisation (National Salvation Associa-
tion) and its subordinate organs are enabled to deceive the
people for their own benefit.

A short time ago, various local circles called for
contributions for the purpose of providing shoes and stock-
ings for the soldiers at the front following receipt of a
telegram in which General Koo, in command of the Third War
Zone, appealed for a sum of $40,000. Towards this sum, the
local banking circles contributed $10,000; the local educa-
tional circles $10,000; and the local industrial and commer-
cial circles $10,000. Seeing that this was a golden
opportunity for them to take undue advantage of the genero-
sity of the public, The People's Front Organization sometime
ago inaugurated an exhibition of articles to be sold for
charity in the Sun Company Building; the exhibits were all
contributed by the general public. Soon the various local
schools followed its example and separately conducted various
forms of charity bazaars from which they derived considerable
profit. According to investigations we have conducted into
their activities, this huge sum of money did not go to the
front, but found its way into the pockets of these unscru-
pulous elements of the People's Front Organisation (The
National Salvation Association). This was the same trick
as that which was used by them during last year in collecting
a number of Chinese relics and artistic products for the
ostensible purpose of holding an exhibition sale for charity
abroad, in order to provide funds for maintaining the
activities of the Communist Party and the People's Front.

Prompted by our own conscience, we responded
enthusiastically every time we were called upon to contribute
what we had in our possession towards the hold/ing exhibitions
of articles for a charity sale, knowing that this was a part
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

人民阵线组织（救国会）及其下属机构借以欺骗民众、谋取私利的自私手段。

不久前，各界收到第三战区司令顾将军来电，呼吁捐款4万元，用于为前线士兵提供鞋袜。为此，本地银行界捐款1万元；教育界捐款1万元；工商界捐款1万元。见有机可乘，可不当利用公众的慷慨，人民阵线组织前一段时间在新新公司大楼发起了一场慈善义卖物品展览；展品均由公众捐赠。不久，本地各学校纷纷效仿，分别举办各种形式的慈善义卖市集，从中获取了可观的利润。根据我们要对其活动进行的调查，这笔巨款并未流向前线，而是落入了人民阵线组织（救国会）这些不肖之徒的口袋。这与他们去年使用的伎俩如出一辙，当时他们收集了一批中国文物和艺术产品，名义上是为了在海外举办慈善义卖展览，实则是为维持共产党和人民阵线的活动筹集资金。

出于良心驱使，每次被号召捐献物品以举办慈善义卖展览时，我们都热情响应，深知这是

page_data.en:
- 3 -
of our duty and that by this the refugees would benefit.
But, alas, we have been deceived every time. But we have
now opened our eyes to their real ends, and we refuse to
assist in any way the present "Exhibition of Articles for
Charity Sale". Such supporters as Messrs. Yu Ya Ching,
H.T. Huang, Ling Kong Hou, and Pan Nying Pao, whose names
have appeared in their regulations, have also realised the
real state of affairs behind their charity project, and have
announced that they would no longer be responsible for the
affairs of the exhibition.
For the purpose of smashing their racket, it is
hoped that local citizens will oppose this exhibition and
refuse to buy any of the exhibits from it.

Shanghai Municipality Refugee Relief Association.
✓（上海市難民救助会）
page_data.zh:
- 3 -
我们责任的一部分，且难民将因此受益。
但是，唉，我们每次都受骗了。但现在我们已看清他们的真实目的，我们拒绝以任何方式协助当前的“慈善义卖物品展览会”。诸如虞洽卿先生、黄汉梁（H.T. Huang）先生、凌孔侯先生和潘宁葆先生等支持者，其名字曾出现在他们的章程中，他们也意识到了其慈善项目背后的真实情况，并宣布不再对展览事务负责。
为了粉碎他们的敲诈勾当，希望本地市民抵制此次展览，拒绝购买其中的任何展品。

上海市难民救济协会。
✓（上海市難民救助会）

page_data.en:
為上海中國職業婦女俱樂部主辦
物品慈善義賣會敬告上海市民
▲揭穿救國會利己分肥黑幕——警告全體市民勿再受欺騙
同胞們！人民陣線組織（即救國會）所發起的上海中國職業婦女俱樂部，（地址在南京路一二號二〇三號房間即福利公司樓上），又在玩什麼「物品慈善義賣」的把戲了，假借波同鄉會為義賣場所。這又是一種完全以欺騙民衆，假慈善的面具而出現的勾當！我們歷經受騙的民衆，為了正義，現在不能不起來揭穿他們的陰謀和肥己的行為！
本來救濟難民的工作，我們應該盡力去做，可是這種艱巨的工作，自應由主管機關統籌辦理，方可防微杜漸，免為一般別具用心的人，假借慈善為名，幹出營私肥己或是其他紛亂的行動。好像國際難民救濟會，上海難民救濟會等組織，就是這一種統一辦理救濟難民的正當團體；他們全由本市法團合法產生或是據根法規組織辦理的，現在人民陣綫（救國會）以及隸屬他們的一切非法組織，所發起的各種義賣——物品慈善義賣就是其中之一——何嘗是為了救濟難民，只是假借一種名義欺騙我們，搾取我們，以滿足他們私囊的一種手段而已！
在過去不久以前，各界曾發起徵募鞋襪捐，說是為了第三戰區顧司令長官來電，籲請滬上接濟四萬元，後由各界募集到三萬元，就中銀行界擔任了一萬元，教育界一萬元，工商界也是一萬元。可是不料人民陣線組織，看到有機可乘，竟藉此名義，發起義賣，向各界徵集物品，不費分文，在大新公司舉行義賣，同時在各學校亦分別發起舉行義賣，收入所得，均甚可觀。但據我們現在調查所得，此項鉅款，全未寄到前方應用，完全給經手人——人民陣線（救國會）份子個人分肥，飽入私囊了，這正同去年以孫夫人名義徵集中國古董藝術品，運往外國義賣同一性質，是供作共產黨和人民陣線的活動經費的。
我們為了救濟難民，受了良心的驅使，在每次義賣徵集物品時，總是踊躍地將自己所珍藏的物品，繼續應徵，聊盡一點國民互救的義務，誰知結果總是被騙，此次「物品慈善義賣會」的勾當，我們是早就洞燭其奸，不願再受他們甘言蜜語的欺騙，已一致予以拒徵，同時他們簡章上所刊的簽名贊助人，如虞洽卿，黃涵之，林康候，潘仰堯等先生，現亦覺悟受愚，分別在聲明脫離，不再負責，我們希望各界對於此輩慣以欺騙民衆向各界徵集物品，以飽私囊的行為，一致起來反對，拒絕購買，民衆們亦一致覺醒，不要買牠，以免再上他們設就了的圈套，這才是真正為難民打算啊！

With reference to diary entry the undersigned, on
27-6-39, proceeded to the Special Branch where infor-
mation relative to this case was elicited as follows:-

On 25-6-39 a letter was received at S.M.P. Head-
quarters from the Vocational Chinese Women's
Lien Hyi Society, Room 203, 102, Nanking Road (Referred
to on diary as Chinese Women's Association) to the
effect that arrangements had been completed with the
Management of the Continental Broadcasting Station
(X.H.H.C.), 351, Peking Road, for the Broadcasting
of a Special programme from the Station between 2 p.m.
and 11 p.m. 29-6-39. The purpose of this programme
was to persuade listeners to purchase vouchers, ex-
changeable for articles which will be offered for sale
in the forthcoming charity bazaar on July 1st, 2nd and
3rd, in the Ningpo Fellow Countrymen's Association, 480,
Yu Ya Ching Road. This programme was examined by
Headquarters and was found to contain nothing objec-
tionable. The fact of the Public being defrauded by
these appeals, as inferred in the threatening letter,
therefore appears absurd.

Enquiries are now proceeding as to whether fric-
tion has been caused between the operators of the two
stations X.H.H.K. and X.H.H.A. as a result of the
society having changed from one to the other with the

of a member of the society being dissatisfied with the
change in stations and consequently may be responsible
for the sending of the letter to X.H.H.K. as a means
of intimidating them against broadcasting further
similar appeals on behalf of the society.
------------------

The scene of this offence (X.H.H.K.) was, as
mentioned in diary 1, registered with the National
Government of China prior to the outbreak of Sino-
Japanese Hostilities. After the retreat of the Chinese
forces from the Shanghai area Mr. Shu, the Proprietor,
refused to have the station registered with the
Japanese, having ignored orders from them to comply with

目前正调查该协会更换广播电台是否导致 X.H.H.K. 和 X.H.H.A. 两家电台运营商之间产生摩擦。此外，也存在该协会某成员因更换电台而不满，进而可能负责向 X.H.H.K. 发送信件，以此恐吓他们不再代表该协会广播类似呼吁的可能性。
------------------

正如日志1所述，本案案发地点（X.H.H.K.）在中日敌对行动爆发前已向中国政府注册。中国军队从上海地区撤退后，业主舒先生拒绝向日本人注册该电台，无视了他们要求 comply with（遵守/配合）的命令

At 11.00 a.m. 26-6-50 Mr. C.J. Keh, manager
of the X... Radio Station, 851 Peking Road,

"I have learned that the Communist Party
is using your station broad-
casting as a safe for merchandise for
their distribution, whereby the
public will be defrauded under the pre-
text of charity.
This letter is to inform you that this
broadcasting must be immediately stopped
otherwise we shall apply drastic action
against you. One round of ammunition
is enclosed as a warning.

(sgd) The Iron & Blood Group
of Youth Anti-Communists
of Chinese Kuomintang".

Da ... Broadcasting Station.

Enquiries by ... and the undersigned

The radio station in question is located on
the 3rd floor of premises, No. 851 Peking Road (south

employs a complement of four males, one female and
two coolies. It is actually owned by Mr. F.S. Shu
General Manager of the Great Eastern Dispensary,

Subject Continental Broadcasting Station - receives instructions
from Radio Broadcasting Control Office.
Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Logan

On the forenoon of June 28, 1939, the
Continental Broadcasting Station (X.H.H.K.), 851
Peking Road, received a telephone message from the
Japanese Radio Broadcasting Control Office instructing
it to detail a representative to the office for
interrogation. Following the receipt of the
telephone message, Charles Madar, the British owner
of the station, went to the Control Office at 3 p.m.
June 28, when he was received by a Japanese who told
him that he should relieve himself of responsibility
for the Continental Broadcasting Station and that
the aerial wire of the Tung Fang (東方) Station
(X.H.H.G.), of which Charles Madar is also the owner,
should be pulled down.

It is to be noted that the Continental
Station was in receipt of a threatening letter
together with a bullet on June 25, 1939 when a
special charity programme was being broadcast from
the Station by the Shanghai Vocational Women's Lien
Nyi Society, while the Tung Fang Station was the
subject of a letter from the Radio Broadcasting
Control Office to the Police requesting the latter
to close it down.

Mr. Charles Madar called at Headquarters
at 11 a.m. June 29, 1939 and confirmed the foregoing.
He also produced a letter (copy attached) which he
received on June 29, 1939, from the Radio Broadcasting
Control Office (also known as Broadcasting Superintendence

you I now beg to request you to close the XHHG Radio

considered to be accepted in this office.

attention.

Yours truly

At 9.30 p.m. June 25, a telephone message was
received from Kuh Tsung Sung ( 葛春 ) of the
Continental Broadcasting Station, X H H K, (K.C.1340),
951 Peking Road, stating that the station had received
a threatening letter at 9.05 p.m. ordering that the
special programme broadcast by the Shanghai Vocational
Chinese Women's Lien Nyi Society, should cease at once,
as it was sponsored by communists and that failure to
comply would result in drastic action being taken.
Kuh Tsung Sung asked what action he should take.
He was informed that he should report the matter to
the Louza Station at once or, as an alternative, to
cease the broadcasting forthwith and report the matter
to this office at 9 a.m. on June 26. In reply he
stated that he would refer the matter to Mr. Hsu Shiao
Chu ( 許曉初 ), General Manager of the Great Eastern
Dispensary, for decision.

The special programme terminated at about 10 p.m.
instead of at 11 p.m. as scheduled.

The matter of the threats received by telephone
was reported to Louza Station by a representative of
the Continental Station on June 26, 1939.

Reference Special Branch report dated June 23,
1939, it will be remembered that this station which
is owned by Charles Madar & Company (British) complained
that its broadcasts are being interfered with by the
broadcasts of Young's Broadcasting Station ( X H H T )
K.C.1320 obtruding on the wave length of the

ascertain the circumstances surrounding the trouble

the Police instructions.

Subject Dah Loh Broadcasting Station reports complaint of obtruding

Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C. Crawford D I
With reference to D.C. (Special Branch's) memo
dated December 10, 1938, (attached hereto) Mr. Yang Yi
Ching (楊慶 ), owner of Young's Broadcasting Station,
was interviewed at Headquarters, on December 12, 1938,
when he was asked if his station had been in receipt of
complaints from listeners concerning interference with
his broadcasts by the broadcasts of any other station.
In reply, Mr. Yang stated that no such complaints had been
received but that about a month ago he found that due to
carelessness by certain of his employees his broadcasts
were not as good as they ought to be. This, however,
was remedied in consequence of his having disciplined
the employees concerned.
Mr. Yang was allowed to leave Headquarters without
any mention being made of the report made by the Dah Loh
Station.

REPORT
Date Dec. 10, 19 38.

Subject......... Deh Loh Broadcasting Station reports complaint of ostruding
received from Young's Broadcasting Station.

Made by... D.S.I. Logan .................... Forwarded by C. Crawford S.J

At 3 p.m. December 9, Mr. Kuh Tsung-sung
(葛春蓀) representing the Dah Loh broadcasting Station,
XHHK, K.C.1340, 851 Peking Road, called at the Special
Branch and made a report to the effect that at 10.30 p.m.
December 8, he received a telephone message from some
person who gave his name as Sung of Young's Broadcasting
Station. Subsequently another person who gave his name
as Zung took Sung's place at the phone and stated in a
hostile tone that Young's Station had received a number
of complaints from listeners to the effect that the
broadcast of the Dah Loh Station was ostruding on the
broadcasts of the former. He emphasized that the Dah
Loh Station should effect adjustment in the equipment
at once, failing which drastic action would be taken
against the Dah Loh Station.

Mr. Kuh Tsung-sung stated that a test subsequently
made by him, showed that it was not his station that was
at fault, but that Young's Station was not properly
adjusted. He further stated that he had effected adjustment
in his equipment in May, 1938, on the instructions of the
Municipal Police (vide report dated 12/5/38)

It is to be noted that the Dah Loh Station is one
of the few Chinese stations which up to the present have
not registered with the Japanese Broadcasting Superintendence
Office. Young's Station, XHHT, K.C.1320, Lane 145, 25
Kuling Road, was established in July, 1938, with permission
from the Broadcasting Superintendence Office.

（批：P.A. to D.C (Sp. Br.)）

事由......... 大乐广播电台转报杨氏广播电台收到的关于干扰的投诉。

呈报人... 特别处督察长 洛根 .................... 转呈人 C. Crawford 高级警司

12月9日下午3时，代表位于北京路851号、呼号XHHK、频率K.C.1340的大乐广播电台的葛春蓀先生（葛春蓀）来到特别处，作出如下报告：12月8日晚上10时30分，他接到一个电话，打电话的人自称是杨氏广播电台的宋（Sung）。随后，另一个自称宗（Zung）的人接替宋接听电话，并以敌对的语气声称，杨氏电台收到许多听众投诉，称大乐电台的广播干扰了前者的广播。他强调，大乐电台应立即调整设备，否则将对大乐电台采取严厉行动。

葛春蓀先生表示，他随后进行的测试表明，故障不在他的电台，而是杨氏电台未适当调整。他还表示，他曾根据警务处的指示（见1938年5月12日的报告）于1938年5月对其设备进行了调整。

值得注意的是，大乐电台是迄今为止尚未向日本广播监理所注册的少数中国电台之一。杨氏电台，呼号XHHT，频率K.C.1320，地址古岭路25号145弄，于1938年7月在获得广播监理所许可后成立。

May 31, 1933.

To the Special Branch, S.M.P.

In accordance with your instructions we changed
our Frequency to 1340 K.C. and have carried on broadcasting
for several days. Owing, however, to the fact that this
frequency is too close to that of the Wha Tung Radio
Station and that it is also the harmonics of the Dah Chung Hwa
Radio Station in the French Concession, we have experienced
serious interference in our broadcasts and complaints have
been repeatedly received from the public. We therefore
beg to request that we be allowed to use the frequency 1320 K.C.
in order to facilitate broadcasting and shall be very grateful
to you for this favour.

Dah Loh Radio Station.

（批：No objection provided no interference with other stations.）

Subject Good Friends Broadcasting Station - commences broadcasting.

Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

The Good Friends Broadcasting Station,
XHHT, K.C. 1360, Lane 77, 12 Kweichow Road, which
was formerly the Hwa Tung Broadcasting Station,
XQHD, 465 Kwangse Road, formally commenced broadcasting
on May 12, 1940, with permission from the Japanese
Broadcasting Superintendent's Office, Hardoon Building,
Nanking Road. Miss Milanowska (Polish) is the owner
and Mr. Pao Ming (包明) is the Chinese Manager.
The removal and change of name was effected
on instructions from the Japanese Superintendent's
Office, as one of the conditions on which permission
to operate was obtained.
At 10.20 a.m. May 14, 1940, Mr. Pao Ming
called at Police Headquarters and produced Certificate
No.10, dated 11/5/40, issued by the Japanese
Superintendent's Office authorizing the Good Friends
Station to broadcast.

Date May 6, 19 40.
Subject... Hwa Tung Radio Station - Dispute over Erection of Antenna.
Made by... D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by... D. I. Crawford

On the forenoon of April 6, 1940, a report
was received from Louza Station regarding a dispute
over the erection of a wireless antenna above the
Yi Hung (怡红) Restaurant, 748 Nanking Road.
D.S.I. Logan and Clerk Wong Chia Tsing attended
and ascertained the following :-
The wireless antenna belongs to the Hwa
Tung Broadcasting Station, 465 Kwangse Road. The
Hwa Tung Station, together with the Dah Loh
Broadcasting Station, 851 Peking Road, were formerly
owned by Charles Madar and Company, 259 Kiangse
Road and not registered with the Japanese Broadcasting
Superintendent's Office. In January, 1940, the
stations were sold to a Miss Milanowska (Polish)
and they suspended broadcasting on April 1, in order
to effect registration with the Japanese. As a
result of negotiations with the Japanese, the latter
is stated to have agreed to grant permission for
the Hwa Tung Station to operate, provided Miss
Milanowska closes the Dah Loh Station and on condition
that the Hwa Tung Station is removed from 465 Kwangse
Road to a new location and changes the call sign.
Consequently, one Loo Foo Zung (鲁虎臣),
in charge of advertising department of the Hwa
Tung Station, was entrusted to find some suitable
premises to which the station could be removed.

1940年4月6日上午，老闸捕房收到一份关于在南京路748号怡红餐厅上方架设无线天线引发纠纷的报告。
副督察长洛根和警员黄家清（Wong Chia Tsing，音译）到场并查明以下情况：
该无线天线属于华通广播电台，原址广西路465号。华通电台连同北京路851号的大乐广播电台，此前均由江西路25号的查尔斯·马达尔公司（Charles Madar and Company）拥有，且未在日本广播监理处注册。1940年1月，这些电台被出售给米拉诺夫斯卡小姐（波兰籍），并于4月1日停止播音，以便向日本方面办理注册。据称，经与日本方面谈判，后者同意许可华通电台运营，条件是米拉诺夫斯卡小姐关闭大乐电台，并将华通电台从广西路465号迁至新址并更改呼号。
因此，华通电台广告部主任鲁虎臣（Loo Foo Zung）受委托寻找合适的场所以便电台搬迁。

Loo approached one of his friends named Sung Wen
Nyi (孫文毅), standing committee member of the
Nanking Road Street Union, Lane 77, 12 Kweichow
Road and solicited his assistance in finding a
suitable place for removal. Through the efforts
of Sung, a room was rented in the Union premises and
in the meantime, a suitable location upon which to
erect the antenna posts was found, one above the
Tai Kong Canned Goods Company, 766-8 Nanking Road
and the other above the Yi Hung Restaurant, 748
Nanking Road. Sung was requested by Loo to approach
these shops for permission for the erection of
the posts. The erection commenced on May 3 but was
objected to on May 5 by Tsai Ts Zung (崔柱臣),
manager and part owner of the Yi Hung Restaurant,
who stated that no permission had been obtained from
him. Tsai Ts Zung received a letter from the Nanking
Road Street Union later on May 5, 1940 formally
requesting his permission to erect the mast and brought
it to Louza Station. A statement taken from Tsai
Ts Zung is attached hereto.

Sung Wen Nyi, when questioned, admitted

尚未获得工部局工务处（I.W.D., S.M.C.）对架设天线的许可，据鲁虎臣称，上海只有少数其他广播电台向工务处申请了必要的许可。

目前无法联系到电台名义上的业主米拉诺夫斯卡小姐以对其进行询问，但调查倾向于表明，这位女士除了名义上之外，与电台事务几乎无关。

虽然缺乏恐吓餐厅业主崔柱臣的确凿证据，但似乎鲁虎臣成功获得了孙文毅的支持，而后者利用其作为南京路街商联合会常务委员的地位，试图获得崔柱臣对架设桅杆的同意，其想法是后者会害怕反对看似得到街商联合会支持的事项。

Tsai Ts Zung (崔桂臣), Manager and part owner
of the Yi Hung Restaurant, 748 Nanking Road. I rented
the house from the landlord about two months ago. The
restaurant has not yet commenced business.
At about 12 noon May 5, 1940, I learned that the
wireless antenna of a radio station was being erected
on the roof of my restaurant without my permission. So
I went to the top and asked who was responsible for the
erection. One of the workers sent for one named Sung
(孫 ) who claimed to be a representative from the
Nanking Road Street Union and who stated that the post
was being erected by the Street Union. I told him
that I objected to the erection of the mast and that
he should first obtain my permission. Sung said that
the Street Union would write me a letter asking
permission to effect the erection. I told him that the
erection must stop as I intended to construct a super-
structure on the roof. The installation however was
continued yesterday, in defiance of my instruction. A
letter asking my permission was delivered to me at 3 p.m.
yesterday, bearing the chop of the Nanking Road Street
Union.
I am strongly opposed to the erection of the post
on the top of my restaurant.

1940年5月5日中午12点左右，我得知一家广播电台的无线天线正在未经我许可的情况下在我的餐厅屋顶上架设。于是我上楼询问谁负责架设。一名工人叫来了一位姓孙（孫）的人，他自称是南京路街商联合会的代表，并称线杆是由街商联合会架设的。我告诉他，我反对架设桅杆，他应该先获得我的许可。孙说街商联合会会给我写一封信请求允许进行架设。我告诉他，因为我打算在屋顶上加建上层结构，所以必须停止架设。然而，昨天他们无视我的指令继续安装。昨天下午3点，我收到了一封请求我许可的信，上面盖有南京路街商联合会的印章。
我强烈反对在我的餐厅顶部架设线杆。

1940年5月6日上午11时，位于南京路748号的倚紅（Yi Hung）餐馆经理兼部分业主崔柱臣（Tsai Ts Zung）来到捕房投诉称，华东（Hwa Tung）广播电台（呼号X.H.H.T.）现正迁至贵州路77弄12号新址，该台在未获其许可的情况下，在其房屋屋顶架设了一根天线桅杆。
经具报人及刑事侦缉队第116号探员调查查明，该广播电台原址位于广西路465号，使用呼号X.Q.H.D.运营，但曾被日本当局勒令关闭并搬迁；日本当局最近已许可该台在贵州路77弄12号重新开播，使用呼号X.H.H.T.。
徐公記（Zee Kung Kyl）铁工厂受雇架设天线，并在房东和租户的许可下，在南京路766号屋顶架设了一根天线桅杆。
1940年5月3日，承包商在未事先获得许可的情况下，开始在投诉人位于南京路748号的房屋屋顶架设另一根天线桅杆。此项指令由直隶路25号義華（Nyi Hwa）药店店主、南京路街道联合会委员沈文儀（Sung Vung Nyce，音译）下达给承包商，此人承担了全部责任。

Complainant first discovered the erection of the
aerial mast on his roof at 12 noon 5-5-40 and questioned
the workers who sent for "Sung" who attended and
informed complainant that the mast was being erected
by the Street Union.

When complainant objected to the erecting of the
mast, "Sung" stated that the "Nanking Road Street Union"
would send him a letter requesting his permission for
the erection.

At 3 p.m. 5-5-40 complainant received a letter
from one Wong Li Jong (王廉公) Chairman of the Nanking
Road Street Union requesting the necessary permission,
but by that time the work of erecting the mast was
already completed.

Further enquiries revealed that one Loo Foo Zung
(盧富成), clerk of the Broadcasting Station was a
friend of "Sung" who used the name of the "Nanking
Road Street Union" to facilitate the erection of the
aerials and the contractors unlawfully entered
complainant's premises to carry out the work without
first obtaining permission.

All concerned were called to Station for questioning
but later released as complainant did not wish to
take any action providing that the aerial mast was
removed from his premises.

The persons concerned agreed to remove the aerial
immediately and the affair was therefore settled
amicably.

W.C. Wilson.

投诉人于1940年5月5日中午12时首次发现其屋顶上架设了天线桅杆，遂质问工人，工人叫来了“沈”（Sung）。“沈”到场后告知投诉人，该桅杆是由街道联合会架设的。

当投诉人对架设桅杆表示反对时，“沈”声称“南京路街道联合会”将致函给他，请求其许可进行架设。

1940年5月5日下午3时，投诉人收到南京路街道联合会主席王廉公（Wong Li Jong）的来信，请求必要的许可，但此时架设桅杆的工作已经完成。

进一步调查查明，广播电台职员盧富成（Loo Foo Zung）是“沈”的朋友，“沈”利用“南京路街道联合会”的名义以便利天线的架设，承包商在未事先获得许可的情况下非法进入投诉人的处所进行施工。

所有相关人员均被召至捕房接受讯问，但因投诉人只要拆除其房屋上的天线桅杆便不愿采取任何行动，故随后将其释放。

相关人员同意立即拆除天线，此事因此得以和平解决。

W.C. 威尔逊（W.C. Wilson）。

A notice appeared in the December 1st issue
of the Sin Wan Pao, to the effect that the Hwa Tung
Broadcasting Station, call sign XQHD, frequency K.C.
1360, located at 465 Kwangse Road, has been sold to Mr.
Charles Madar of Charles Madar & Co., 259 Kiangse Road,
transfer of ownership to take effect from December 1st.
Mr. Charles Madar (British) when communicated
with, confirmed the above information and stated that
the deed of sale is registered at H.B.M. Consulate-General.
Mr. J.F. Ford of H.B.M. Consulate-General, who was
interviewed at 2 p.m. December 1st, by D.S.I. Logan,
produced a copy of the deed of sale which was deposited
at the Consulate-General for the purpose of record.
At 3 p.m. December 1st, Mr. N.A. Ivanow,
Attorney and Counsellor-at-Law, 153-L Route des Soeurs,
Apt. 53, visited the Special Branch and handed in a copy
of the deed of sale (attached hereto)
The Hwa Tung Broadcasting Station is one of the
group of Chinese radio stations, originally totalling
seven in number, which were operating under permits
issued by the National Government of China, prior
to the outbreak of the local Sino-Japanese hostilities.
At 9 p.m. June 12, 1938, an unexploded hand
grenade was found about 5 feet from the entrance to the
Hwa Tung Station.

to bear on the Hwa Tung and other stations referred to
above, to persuade them to register with the Japanese

值得注意的是，该信函中还指出，日本方面打算将目前由华东电台使用的波长分配给将由某些日本人和外国人建立的几家新电台之一。

伊万诺夫先生在上述特别部门的会谈中提到，出于礼节，他的委托人、华东电台的新业主马达尔先生，打算将所有权转移一事通知日本广播监理处。

BRITISH CONCERN TAKES OVER THE HWA TUNG
BROADCASTING STATION

An advertisement appearing in the "Sin Wan
Pao" to-day announces that Charles Madar, owner of Madar
& Company 麥達洋行 (a British concern), will assume
proprietorship over the Hwa Tung Broadcasting Station
(華東電台) with effect from December 1, 1938.

in the British Consulate under certificate No. 605. Madar
& Company will be responsible for all the liabilities of
the Hwa Tung Broadcasting Station from December 1, 1938.

Subject Liang Yue Broadcasting Station (Swiss) (XQCT) - wavelength
K.C. 1300 changed to K.C. 1460.
Made by D.S.I. Logan Forwarded by C Gordon

The attached letter dated February 16, 1939, from Major K. Asano of the Radio Broadcast Control Office, was received at Headquarters, on February 18, 1939 announcing that the Liang Yue Broadcasting Station (XQCT) K.C. 1300 has registered with the Japanese authorities and that the wavelength has been changed from K.C. 1300 to K.C.1460 as from February 16, 1939.

At 11 a.m. February 18, Mr. Saunier (Swiss), owner of the Station called at the Special Branch and confirmed the change in wavelength. Mr. Saunier stated that due to loss of business in consequence of interference with his broadcasts by the Skylark (Tien Chuan) Station (XQHG), owned by F.W. Wettengel (German), he had no other alterantive but to register with the Japanese Authorities and effect the change as instructed by the latter. In course of the negotiations relating to registration, he was asked to sign an apology prepared by the Japanese Radio Broadcast Control Office but refused to do so.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE / 20 FEB. 1939）

From the foregoing it will be seen that this is one more instance of Japanese interference with the rights of a foreigner who is of a nationality which enjoys extra-territoriality.

主题 良友广播电台（瑞士籍）(XQCT) - 波长从1300千周变更为1460千周。
由 D.S.I. Logan 制作 由 C Gordon 转呈

总部于1939年2月18日收到无线电广播管制办公室浅野大佐（Major K. Asano）1939年2月16日的来函，宣布良友广播电台（XQCT）1300千周已向日本当局注册，且自1939年2月16日起，波长已从1300千周变更为1460千周。

2月18日上午11时，该电台所有人 Saunier 先生（瑞士籍）到访特务科，证实了波长的变更。Saunier 先生表示，由于德国人 F.W. Wettengel 所有的云雀（天传）电台（XQHG）对其广播造成干扰，导致业务损失，他别无选择，只能向日本当局注册并按其指示进行变更。在与注册相关的谈判过程中，他被要求签署一份由日本无线电广播管制办公室拟定的道歉信，但他拒绝签署。

（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / 总监办公室 / 1939年2月20日）

由此可见，这是日本人干涉享有治外法权的外国人权利的又一例证。

Mr. S. Uyenara,
Deputy Commissioner,
S. M. P.

Sir,

With regard to the control of privately
owned radio broadcast stations in the Settlement, which
has been receiving your kind attention for some time,
it has already been agreed between your office and this
administration that in the event of an application being
received for the establishment of a new station, first
of all this administration will institute enquiries and
should it be found to conform in every detail with the
required standard, such application will be referred to
you for further examination from Police point of view.
If there is no objection on your part, the application
will be referred back to us for the final approval for
registration. This is the procedure being followed
to-day.

A German subject named Wettengel applied to this
office under date of September 7, 1938 for the establish-
ment of a new radio station in Yu Ya Ching Road broad-
casting under carrier frequency of 1,300 kc. and power
of 100 w. After the necessary enquiries, this application
was approved by this office with effect from to-day.
Meanwhile, an advertisement appeared in the Sin Van Ya Pao
dated 27.9.38 announcing the opening of a new station
known as Liang Yue Broadcasting Station(兩友電台)
operated by the Zeu Hwa & Co.(瑞華公司), the frequency
and power quoted being 1,300 kc and 200 w respectively.
This station has no authority whatsoever to operate and
in keeping with the policy of exercising effective control
over all stations, it will be ordered by us to close down.

关于租界内私营广播电台的管制问题，承蒙贵处一段时间以来的关注，贵我双方已达成协议：一旦收到建立新电台的申请，首先由本行政机构进行调查，若发现其在各方面均符合规定标准，则将申请转交贵处，从警务角度进行进一步审查。若贵处无异议，申请将退回本处以获得最终的注册批准。这是目前遵循的程序。

一名名为 Wettengel 的德国臣民于1938年9月7日向本办公室申请在虞洽卿路建立一个新的广播电台，载波频率为1,300 kc，功率为100 w。经必要调查后，本办公室已批准该申请，自今日起生效。与此同时，1938年9月27日的《新闻报》(Sin Van Ya Pao) 上刊登了一则广告，宣布一家名为“两友广播电台”的新电台开业，由瑞华公司 (Zeu Hwa & Co.) 运营，所称频率和功率分别为1,300 kc 和 200 w。该电台没有任何运营授权，为贯彻对所有电台实施有效管制的政策，我们将命令其关闭。

同时，我 hereby 申请获准开设并运营一家商业及音乐广播电台，该台将安装在芝罘路（Chili Road）25号二楼的两间房间内。

广播语言为中文和英文。

电台由我直接管理，商业管理由专家顾宜华（Kou Yi Hoa）( ) 负责，并由我的儿子协助。

电台呼号为 X. Q. C. T.。

波长 1060 或 1300（200瓦）。

恳请阁下指示我 regarding 工部局规章所需办理的手续，并预先致谢，

此致，

尊敬的先生，

您忠实的，

J. V. Saunier.

CONSULAT GENERAL DE SUISSE
SHANGHAI
Pour toute la Chine

Shanghai September 8th
1938

Reference S.XII.B.236.-2629

Dear Sir,

I beg to acknowledge receipt of your letter
of September 6th, informing me that you intend to
install and run a broadcasting station at No 25 Chili
Road, As requested, I am enclosing herewith a letter
of recommendation for the purpose of registration with
the competent authorities of the Shanghai Municipal
Council.

As already explained to you verbally, my
consent in this matter is strictly conditional on your
refraining from any and all transmissions of a
political nature from the said radio-station.

1 enclosure

Yours faithfully,

Emile Fontanel

Swiss Consul General.

J. V. Saunier, Esq.,
Shanghai.
page_data.zh:
瑞士驻上海总领事馆
全中国

上海，1938年9月8日

参考号 S.XII.B.236.-2629

尊敬的先生：

谨确认收到您9月6日的来信，获悉您打算在芝罘路（Chili Road）25号安装并运营一座广播电台。应您的要求，兹随函附上一封推荐信，以便向上海公共租界工部局主管当局注册。

正如此前口头向您解释的那样，我对此事的同意严格取决于您不从该广播电台传输任何具有政治性质的内容。

附件 1 份

此致，

敬礼，

Emile Fontanel

瑞士总领事。

J. V. Saunier 先生，
上海。

CONSULAT GÉNÉRAL DE SUISSE
EN CHINE
S-XII.B.236.- 2630

Shanghai, September 8th 1938.

Sir,

At the request of Mr.J.V.Saunier, a Swiss
citizen, aged 47 years, registered with this
Consulate-General, I have the honour to let you
know that there is no objection on the part of
this Consulate-General for his working of a
broadcasting station, which he intends to open
at 25 Chili Road, Shanghai, under the call-name
X Q C T. Mr.Saunier undertakes to refrain from
any radio-transmissions of a political nature.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

SWISS CONSUL-GENERAL

The Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
S h a n g h a i .

Another “Exhibition of Articles for Charity Sale” is now

the people behind the mask of charity. For the sake of justice,

The task of giving relief to refugees, we should indeed

as it does no amall amount of difficulties, should be handled

bility ef unscrupulous elements seeking their own selfish ends 
under the guise of and in the name of charity, may be excluéed. 
Organisations such as the International Relief Committee, and 
the Shanghai Refugee Relief Association, are the proper organs 
responsible for the relief of refugees; they have been brought 
into being by local respectable civil organs and are being 
maintained in accordance with legal principles. The present 
exhibition of articles for a charity sale, and other forme of 
charity basaars are nothing more than the sefish means whereby 


the People's Front Organisation (National Salvation Assecia- 
tion) and its subordinate organs are enabled to deceive the 
people for their own benefit.

contributions for the purpose of providing shoes and steck- 
ings for the soldiers at the front following receipt of a 
telegram in which General Koo, in command of the Third War 
Zone, appealed for a sum of $40,000. Towards this sum, the 
local banking circles contributed $10,000; the local educa- 
tional circles $10,000; and the local industrial and comer- 
cial circles $10,000. Seeing that this was a golden 
opportunity for them to take undue advantage of the geners- 
sity of the public, The People's Front Organization sometime 
ago inaugurated an exhibition of articles to be sold for 
charity in the Sun Company Building; the exhibits were ali

as that which was used by then during last year im collecting

abread, in order to provide funds for maintaining the
